captions.instagram:
How do large language models (LLMs) work?

Every chatbot answer is built one guess at a time. Train a real tiny language model on a paragraph about monsoons and chai, watch a tokenizer chop Hindi into bytes, click a word to see what it attends to, and catch the model saying something false with total confidence.

→ A language model does one thing: it guesses the next piece of text, again and again.
→ Temperature decides how daring it is: low plays safe, high gets wild.
→ Models read tokens, not letters. Merging common pairs turns bytes into word pieces.
→ Hindi letters take 3 bytes each, so English-trained tokenizers often need many more tokens.
→ Each word becomes a point in space. Words used in similar ways land close together.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/llmclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How do large language models (LLMs) work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Every chatbot answer is built one guess at a time. Train a real tiny language model on a paragraph about monsoons and chai, watch a tokenizer chop Hindi into bytes, click a word to see what it attends to, and catch the model saying something false with total confidence.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/llmclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/llmclear

In this video:
• A machine that guesses the next word. A language model gives a probability to every possible next piece of text.
• Text becomes tokens. Models read numbered pieces called tokens, built by byte-pair encoding: start from 256 bytes and keep merging the commonest pair.
• Words become points in space. Each token is swapped for an embedding, a long list of numbers.
• Attention: words look at words. In a transformer, every token makes a query, a key and a value.
• Scale, then teaching. Big models have billions of parameters, trained on trillions of tokens to predict the next one, then tuned on examples and human feedback to be helpful.
• Fluent is not the same as true. Because they predict likely text, LLMs can state false things with full confidence, repeat bias and sometimes repeat training text.
